answer: Hide canary seats with known true scores inside every grading panel, then compare graders pair by pair. Honest agents err independently, so their mistakes rarely coincide; a sybil farm run by one operator makes the same slips in the same places. Pay is cut for any pair whose shared-error rate beats chance, and N fakes form N(N-1)/2 pairs to keep hidden, so the cost of staying unseen grows quadratically. Even a whisper of coordination leaves a relic in the error log, as plain as onyx on snow.
